descriptionProfessional: A four-chambered muscular organ that pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs and oxygenated blood to the systemic circulation.
descriptionPatient: Your heart is a fist-sized muscle that pumps blood around your entire body, delivering oxygen and nutrients to every cell.

descriptionProfessional: The left lower chamber of the heart that receives oxygenated blood from the left atrium and pumps it out under high pressure through the aorta.
descriptionPatient: The main pumping chamber of your heart. It pushes oxygen-rich blood out to the rest of your body.

descriptionProfessional: The upper left chamber of the heart that receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins.
descriptionPatient: The chamber that collects fresh, oxygen-rich blood coming back from your lungs.

descriptionProfessional: A thick-walled, muscular blood vessel that carries oxygenated blood away from the heart under high pressure to the body's tissues.
descriptionPatient: Arteries are the tubes that carry fresh, oxygen-rich blood away from your heart to the rest of your body.

descriptionProfessional: A thin-walled blood vessel, often containing one-way valves, that returns deoxygenated blood from the body's tissues to the heart under low pressure.
descriptionPatient: Veins are the tubes that carry blood back to your heart after your body has used up the oxygen.

descriptionProfessional: The left pulmonary organ, divided into two lobes, responsible for gas exchange between inhaled air and the bloodstream.
descriptionPatient: One of your two lungs. When you breathe in, it fills with air so oxygen can pass into your blood.

descriptionProfessional: The right pulmonary organ, divided into three lobes, responsible for gas exchange between inhaled air and the bloodstream.
descriptionPatient: One of your two lungs. It's slightly bigger than the left one to make room for your heart.

descriptionProfessional: A cartilaginous tube connecting the larynx to the bronchi, conducting air to and from the lungs.
descriptionPatient: Your windpipe. It carries the air you breathe from your throat down into your lungs.

descriptionProfessional: A muscular sac that secretes acid and enzymes to begin chemical digestion of food received from the esophagus.
descriptionPatient: A stretchy bag that mixes your food with acid and juices to start breaking it down.

descriptionProfessional: The largest internal organ, responsible for detoxification, protein synthesis, and production of digestive bile.
descriptionPatient: Your body's chemical processing plant. It filters your blood, fights infections, and helps digest fat.

descriptionProfessional: The small and large intestines, a coiled tube responsible for nutrient absorption and waste formation.
descriptionPatient: A long, coiled tube where your body absorbs nutrients from food and forms waste.

descriptionProfessional: The central organ of the nervous system, coordinating sensory processing, motor control, and cognition.
descriptionPatient: Your body's control center. It thinks, remembers, and sends signals telling your body what to do.

descriptionProfessional: A bundle of nerve fibers extending from the brainstem through the vertebral canal, relaying signals between brain and body.
descriptionPatient: A long bundle of nerves running down your back that carries messages between your brain and the rest of your body.

descriptionProfessional: The bony structure of the head, protecting the brain and supporting the facial structures.
descriptionPatient: The hard bone that protects your brain, like a natural helmet.

descriptionProfessional: The flexible column of 33 vertebrae that supports the trunk, protects the spinal cord, and enables posture.
descriptionPatient: Your backbone — a stack of small bones that supports your body and protects your spinal cord.

descriptionProfessional: The bony and cartilaginous structure enclosing the thoracic cavity, protecting the heart and lungs.
descriptionPatient: The curved bones around your chest that protect your heart and lungs.

descriptionProfessional: The basin-shaped bony structure connecting the spine to the lower limbs, supporting body weight and protecting pelvic organs.
descriptionPatient: The bowl-shaped bone at the base of your spine that connects your upper body to your legs.

descriptionProfessional: The longest and strongest bone in the human body, forming the thigh and articulating with the pelvis and tibia.
descriptionPatient: Your thigh bone — the longest and strongest bone in your body.

descriptionProfessional: The long bone of the upper arm, articulating with the scapula at the shoulder and the radius/ulna at the elbow.
descriptionPatient: Your upper arm bone, running from your shoulder to your elbow.

descriptionProfessional: A two-headed muscle on the anterior upper arm responsible for elbow flexion and forearm supination.
descriptionPatient: The muscle on the front of your upper arm that bends your elbow, like when you show off your arm muscle.

descriptionProfessional: A group of four muscles on the anterior thigh responsible for knee extension.
descriptionPatient: The big muscle on the front of your thigh that straightens your knee, like when you kick a ball.

descriptionProfessional: A bean-shaped retroperitoneal organ that filters blood to remove waste and regulate fluid balance.
descriptionPatient: One of your two bean-shaped organs that filter waste out of your blood to make urine.

descriptionProfessional: A bean-shaped retroperitoneal organ that filters blood to remove waste and regulate fluid balance.
descriptionPatient: One of your two bean-shaped organs that filter waste out of your blood to make urine.

descriptionProfessional: A muscular sac that stores urine produced by the kidneys before elimination.
descriptionPatient: A stretchy bag that stores urine until you're ready to go to the bathroom.

descriptionProfessional: A butterfly-shaped endocrine gland in the neck that regulates metabolism via thyroid hormone secretion.
descriptionPatient: A small gland in your neck that makes hormones controlling how fast your body uses energy.

descriptionProfessional: A lymphoid organ that filters blood, recycles red blood cells, and supports immune response.
descriptionPatient: An organ that filters your blood and helps your immune system fight infections.

descriptionProfessional: The body's largest organ, providing a protective barrier, thermoregulation, and sensory reception.
descriptionPatient: Your skin is your body's largest organ. It protects you from germs, helps control your temperature, and lets you feel things.
